venue.name: Maritime Museum of British Columbia
venue.description: The Maritime Museum of BC is at 744 Douglas Street in downtown Victoria, close to the Inner Harbour. It describes its current home as a smaller temporary location of two rooms while it looks for a larger permanent space, and most visitors spend well under an hour there. Exhibits cover the maritime history of British Columbia, with a gift shop, children's activity books, a colouring station and a research space. For groups it runs four booked school programs, at the museum, in your own classroom or online, and takes self guided bookings for groups of eight or more.

facility_notes.washrooms: We have a gender inclusive, single stall washroom available that has a baby change table. While this should be large enough for a standard wheelchair to fit in, a motorized wheelchair will not.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Our exhibit space is accessible for standard and motorized wheelchairs. We have push-button door openers on both our entrance and office doors.
facility_notes.lunch_space: While we don't offer food or beverages for sale, you're more than welcome to bring along non-messy snacks.
facility_notes.bus_parking: The closest city parkade is under the Central Branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library on Broughton Street. There is also street parking nearby.

restrictions: Children under the age of 12 must be accompanied by a paying adult (aged 18+) for all visits, programs, and workshops.
Pets are welcome. We ask that they remain on a leash at all times.
venue.hours_notes: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Closed Sept. 3 to 8 to run the Classic Boat Festival in Victoria's Inner Harbour. Check the events calendar for other hours notices.

programs.name: Pollution Solutions
programs.description: A 90 minute school program about where fresh water comes from, the water cycle, and pollution. Children consider how the oceans and water are connected to them and what keeps water clean, and the museum says they leave with tangible ways to keep the ocean healthy. It is offered at the museum for $150 for the group, or in your own classroom for $200. Up to 30 students per program.
programs.what_children_do: Children start together in the middle of the room for a land acknowledgement and a presentation, doing activities as a group along the way. They then split into two groups and rotate through stations, before coming back together at the end to talk about what they found.
programs.our_note: This is the only one of the four topics written for the youngest classes. The price is for the whole booking rather than per child, so a class of 12 pays the same as a class of 30. Adults may be given a job to do during the stations, so bring people who are happy to join in.
programs.practical_summary: Ninety minutes for up to 30 children, with a washroom and a baby change table on site and step free access for standard wheelchairs. There is no lunch room and nothing published about bus parking, so plan where to eat and where the bus waits.
programs.extra_fees_note: School and group bookings have a non-refundable $10 deposit to hold your date.
programs.payment_timing: A non refundable $10 deposit holds the date. They confirm the reservation by email within 3 to 5 working days and invoice the rest of the cost.
programs.cancellation_note: If we cancel a program, you will receive a full refund of your deposit. If you need to cancel or rebook, tell us within 48 hours prior to the start of the program to move your date. If you are a no-show, your $10 deposit will not be refunded.
curriculum_tags: BC Social Studies, Kindergarten to Grade 1

programs.name: In Search of Equality: Deconstructing Immigration Experiences to the West Coast of BC
programs.description: A 90 minute school program on immigration to the west coast. Students reflect on what it means to be Canadian, work through a suitcase activity, and consider the legacy of discriminatory immigration policies. The museum lists it for grades 4 to 6 social studies and also for grade 9. It runs at the museum for $150 for the group, in your classroom for $200, or online for $100. Up to 30 students.
programs.what_children_do: Children think and talk about what being Canadian means to them, work through a suitcase activity that asks them to put themselves in the place of a refugee, and discuss how past immigration rules affected people's lives.
programs.our_note: Serious subject matter handled through a suitcase activity, so it suits a class that can sit with a hard topic. The museum also lists it for grade 9, so it stretches further than the grade band on the card suggests. The price covers the booking, not each child.
programs.practical_summary: Ninety minutes for up to 30 children, with a washroom and a baby change table on site and step free access for standard wheelchairs. There is no lunch room and nothing published about bus parking, so plan where to eat and where the bus waits.

programs.name: Voyages to the Coast: Sails, Savvy and the Spirit of Curiosity
programs.description: A 90 minute school program on exploration and early European expeditions to the west coast, and their impact on people, ecosystems and culture. Children then practise sea skills such as knot tying and navigation. It runs at the museum for $150 for the group, in your classroom for $200, or online for $100. Up to 30 students.
programs.what_children_do: Children talk about what the word explore means to them, hear about early expeditions to this coast and what they changed, then practise sea skills by tying knots and trying navigation.
programs.our_note: Knot tying and navigation make this the most hands on of the four topics. If the bus is the problem, this is one of the three they will bring to your classroom. The price covers the booking, not each child.

programs.name: Furs, Forts, and Fervour: The Impact and Legacy of Contact
programs.description: A 90 minute school program on the Hudson's Bay Company and its impact on Indigenous Peoples, settlers and the land. Children examine real otter and beaver pelts, a Hudson's Bay blanket and other trade items. It runs at the museum for $150 for the group or online for $100, and is the one topic they do not bring to your classroom. Up to 30 students.
programs.what_children_do: Children handle real otter and beaver pelts, a Hudson's Bay blanket and other objects from the trade, and talk about how society, economy and environment were tied together and what the company left behind.
programs.our_note: This is the one with real pelts and a blanket to handle, so it works well for a class that needs something in front of them. It does not travel to schools, so it is the museum or a video session. The price covers the booking, not each child.

programs.name: Outreach visit to your classroom
programs.description: The museum will bring a school program to your classroom for $200 for the group. Three of the four topics travel: Pollution Solutions for kindergarten to grade 2, In Search of Equality for grades 4 to 6 and grade 9, and Voyages to the Coast for grades 4 to 6. Each is 90 minutes for up to 30 students. Furs, Forts, and Fervour is offered at the museum and online only.
programs.what_children_do: The same program runs in your own classroom, so children stay in a room they know. What they handle depends on which of the three travelling topics you pick, from water cycle stations to a suitcase activity to knot tying.
programs.our_note: Useful when the bus is the thing standing in your way. It costs $50 more than coming to the museum, and only three of the four topics travel, so check that the one you want is on the list. The site does not say what they need from your room, so ask when you book.
programs.practical_summary: They come to you, so your own washrooms, lunch space and room are what the day rests on. What they need set up, and how much notice they want for a school visit, are not published, so ask when you book.

programs.name: Virtual field trip
programs.description: A live online version of a school program, $100 for the group. Three topics are offered this way: In Search of Equality for grades 4 to 6 and grade 9, Voyages to the Coast for grades 4 to 6, and Furs, Forts, and Fervour for grades 4 to 9. Each is listed as 90 minutes for up to 30 students. The site does not say which video platform is used or what you need at your end.
programs.our_note: The cheapest way in at $100 for the whole group, and it suits a class that cannot travel. Nothing is published about the platform or what has to work in your room, so settle that well before the day.
programs.practical_summary: This one runs over video, so nothing at the museum affects your day. What you need at your end is not published, so ask when you book.

programs.name: Self guided group visit
programs.description: Groups go through the gallery at their own pace, with interactive exhibits, a scavenger hunt and self guided activity books available for all ages. The group rate is $4 for children and youth under 17 and $7.50 for adults and seniors. Designated aides are free and Leisure Assistance Pass holders get 80 percent off. Groups of eight or more are asked to book through the booking form with the date, time, group size and age category.
programs.what_children_do: Children move through the two gallery rooms at their own pace, look at the exhibits and try the interactive ones, work through a scavenger hunt and fill in an activity book.
programs.our_note: The museum is two rooms and most people are through in half an hour to an hour, so this works better as one stop in a downtown morning than as the whole outing. Groups of eight or more still have to book ahead even though nobody is guiding you. This is the price per child, not per group.
programs.practical_summary: A washroom with a baby change table on site, step free for standard wheelchairs, and snacks are allowed although there is nowhere set aside to sit and eat. There is nothing published about bus parking, so sort out drop off before the day.
programs.extra_fees_note: Designated aides are free. Leisure Assistance Pass holders get 80% off.
programs.evidence: For groups of 8+, please book through our booking form with the date, time, group size, and age category of your self-guided visit.

programs.name: Private Mini Mariners for your group
programs.description: Mini Mariners is an ongoing Saturday program that is included in adult admission or membership. The museum says a group can book a private Mini Mariners session through the booking form. What a private booking costs, how long it lasts and which ages it suits are not published.
programs.our_note: This is the one thing on the site aimed at young children rather than school classes, so it is worth asking about if your group is under five. Neither the price nor the age range is published, so ask for both, and ask what the children actually do in the session.
programs.practical_summary: Same building as any visit, with a washroom and a baby change table and step free access for standard wheelchairs. The cost, the length and the ages it suits are all unpublished, so this one needs a phone call or an email.
programs.evidence: To book a private Mini Mariners program for your group, use the booking form.

gaps: General admission is free for children under 12, but only up to four children per paying adult, and each extra child is $3. A group of eight or more books the group rate instead, which is $4 per child.
No days or start times are published for school programs. Bookings run off their calendar, and they say to email if the date you want is not listed.
No minimum notice is published for a booking. They say only that they confirm within 3 to 5 working days of the deposit.
Whether the program prices include tax is not stated.
There is no lunch room. Non messy snacks are allowed but nowhere is set aside to eat, so plan lunch elsewhere.
Nothing is published about bus parking or drop off. The only parking mentioned is the library parkade on Broughton Street and street parking.
The cost, the length and the age range of a private Mini Mariners booking are all unpublished.
The site mentions Museum Tots activities on Saturdays in one place and Mini Mariners in another. It is not clear whether these are the same program.
The online booking product is labelled 2025, so it is worth confirming the prices still stand when you book.
The self guided group rate has no upper group size, and the museum describes itself as two rooms, so ask how many children they can take at once.
The homepage social image is a photograph with no alt text, so the exterior photograph on the visit page, which carries the site's own description, was used as the main image instead.
Two of the photographs have no alt text on the site, so their descriptions were written after opening each image in a browser and looking at it.
